title: Fernando Cerimedo’s International Network Includes the PRI and Sí por México
author: Aníbal García Fernández
content:
_This article by[Aníbal García
Fernández](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anibal/) originally appeared in
the [October 3, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/investigacion/red-internacional-de-
fernando-cerimedo-incluye-al-pri-y-si-por-mexico/), a Mexican investigative
journalism magazine._

_The downfall of Fernando Cerimedo—prosecuted in Bolivia for crimes related to
attempted femicide and_ money laundering _—has led to the destabilization of
some interventionist strategies promoted by United States agencies. The
international network of the main partner of Javier Negre, in_ La Derecha
Diario,_is linked to Mexico through the PRI, through the structure of Sí Por
México—promoted by businessman Claudio X González and former right-wing
candidate Xochitl Gálvez—and through Alonso Cedeño. The latter shares spaces
with Dick Morris, one of the creators of the biggest smear campaign against
López Obrador: the "danger to Mexico" campaign_

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-00.jpg)Illustration: Gemini AI / Contralínea

The case of Fernando Cerimedo—co-owner with Javier Negre of _La Derecha
Diario_ —shows the new forms taken by destabilization sponsored by United
States agencies, and the relationships among the Latin American right. Its
epicenter is in Miami, and it connects with Latin America.

This international network, woven by the former adviser to the presidents of
Argentina, Javier Milei, and Bolivia, Rodrigo Paz, reaches the structure of
the Mexican electoral right, through connections with the Institutional
Revolutionary Party and the political platform Sí por México, sponsored by
businessman Claudio X González Guajardo—shareholder of the transnational paper
company Kimberly Clark—and which connects to former presidential candidate
Xóchitl Gálvez.

Criminally prosecuted in Bolivia for the attempted femicide of his former
partner Nadia Beller and on matters of alleged _money laundering_ , Fernando
Cerimedo heads an international political and media network dedicated to
destabilizing governments, in coordination with interventionist strategies
promoted by United States agencies.

_La Derecha Diario_ represents just one of its phalanxes. In the Mexican case,
it is linked to the PRI leadership and the structure of Sí Por México; it also
reaches Alonso Cedeño, who shares spaces with Dick Morris, one of the creators
of one of the biggest smear campaigns against Andrés Manuel López Obrador, in
the context of the 2006 election.

**Dick Morris was the mind behind the _slogan_ "López Obrador is a danger to
Mexico,"** together with the Spaniard Antonio Solá and Maximiliano Cortázar.
Today, this figure who did so much harm to Mexico **is part of that Cerimedo
network, which extends to Xochitl Gálvez, Sí por México and Claudio X
González**.

**The link between Fernando Cerimedo, Dick Morris and Claudio X González is
Alonso Ernesto Cedeño Gutiérrez** , someone who took part in the school that
Dick Morris formed together with Cerimedo and**Andrés "Andy" Rivas, who is an
adviser to the president of Paraguay and representative of the University of
Florida in Uruguay, through the Adam Smith Institute**.

Dick Morris, who was also an adviser to Bill Clinton, founded the Dick Morris
Academy in 2025, where several political advisers teach courses. Among them
are Luis Rosales, Ángel Beccassimo, _Andy_ Rivas, Fernando Cerimedo and the
Mexican Alonso Cedeño.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-02.png)Source: Dick Morris Academy, 2025

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-03.jpg)

**The link with Alonso Cedeño connects, in turn, with the PRIAN 's former
presidential candidate, Xochitl Gálvez, and the Sí por México platform.
**Proof of this is a **legal proceeding opened in 2021 before the Electoral
Tribunal of the Federal Judiciary, brought against Alonso Cedeño**.

Case file SRE-PSC-191/2021[1] was filed by the Morena party, which denounced
**the dissemination of content related to the recall process, published on Sí
Por México 's social media**, where they called on people not to take part in
that vote. **What matters about this document is that it exposes that the
person responsible for Sí por México 's posts was Cedeño, who shares spaces
with Dick Morris, Fernando Cerimedo and _Andy_ Rivas.**

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-04.png)

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-05.png)Source: Electoral Tribunal of the Federal Judiciary, 2021.

As for the connection with the **Institutional Revolutionary Party, it comes
through Cedeño** , who has been invited on several occasions to teach courses
at the Reyes Heroles Institute.**Led by Alejandro Moreno** , the PRI remains
an open opponent of the fourth transformation and even openly promotes foreign
interventionism, especially by the United States: _Alito_ Moreno constantly
travels to the neighboring country to the north and opens the doors of the
Senate to Larry Rubin, so that he can promote a pro-US agenda, as happened
recently with the debate on the dual nationality reforms for candidacies.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-06.png)

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-07.jpg)Source: Reyes Heroles Institute

**In addition, Cerimedo 's network of friends, especially through Dick Morris
and _Andy_ Rivas, keeps close to other political actors of the PRIAN: **Rivas
is director of the Adam Smith Center in Uruguay, an extension of the right in
Miami, since it is an appendage of Florida International University.

This last institution has invited right-wing politicians as speakers, such as
former Mexican president Felipe Calderón; but also Juan Guaidó, Álvaro Uribe,
Iván Duque and Mauricio Macri.

In that connection with the international and Cuban right, Alessandra Rojo de
la Vega, Mauricio Tabe and Jorge Romero, of the National Action Party,
recently attended the Miami 2026 Mayors Summit.

### Damián Merlo, LAAG and Milei

Investigations by the Media Observatory of _Cubadebate_ and by Argentine media
have mapped part of Fernando Cerimedo's international structure, and reveal
how the ultra-right networks operate in Miami, [capital of the Latin American
right](https://www.oblawfare.org/post/milei-y-noboa-en-miami-red-de-derechas-
latinoamericanas).

As _Cubadebate_ highlighted, in 2023 the link became explicit between
**Fernando Cerimedo as CEO of the lobbying firm Numen and the firm of his
partner Damián Merlo, managing partner of Latin America Advisory Group
(LAAG)**. The link, moreover, involved a contract to collaborate with the
campaign of Argentina's president, Javier Milei, who in 2024 traveled to Miami
to be recognized as "international ambassador of light."

The propaganda plan in favor of Milei consisted of "preparing op-eds,
connecting members of the House and the Senate," and **outreach to _think
tanks_ such as Heritage, the Center for Strategic and International Studies
(CSIS), the Council on Foreign Relations and the Atlantic Council**.

As an example, **in 2024 Milei visited the Council on Foreign Relations** in
the midst of the UN General Assembly. At the CFR he gave a closed-door talk.
He also held his third meeting with Elon Musk, visited Wall Street, and met
with Ursula von der Leyen and Daniel Noboa.

**In 2025, Milei received the Global Citizen Award 2025 from the hand of the
Treasury secretary** at a gala dinner of the **Atlantic Council**. That same
year, Milei received at the Casa Rosada Kevin Roberts, president of the
Heritage Foundation; its head of Latin America, Andrés Martínez Fernández; the
head of the Index of Economic Freedom, Buhm Jung KIM; and the foundation's
chief of staff, Ryan Neuhaus.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-08.jpg)Source: Casa Rosada, 2025 [2]

In the midst of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in Washington in
2026, Argentina's ambassador Alec Oxenford took part in a meeting between Meta
and CSIS on artificial intelligence, an element that generates controversy in
Argentina.

### Damian Merlo and Bukele

But it was not only Milei: **the Latin American right saw in Cerimedo and
Merlo two people who could open the doors of US elite circles for them.** In
the case of **Nayib Bukele, president of El Salvador, a so-called outsider,
also of the right, he paid Merlo 's firm more than 2.5 million dollars between
2021 and 2025.** And **for 2026 a contract was signed for 780 thousand dollars
to be paid in monthly installments**.

**According to US government data, the Compañía de Luz Eléctrica de Ahuachapán
SA is the one that signed the contract with LAAG**.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-09.jpg)

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-10.jpg)

According to the documents, **the government of Nayib Bukele, characterized by
violating human rights through the Territorial Control Plan** , designed by
the Venezuelan Santiago Rosas of Lab-Co (Collaborative Public Policy Solutions
Laboratory), **paid for the services of Fernando Cerimedo 's
partner**—investigated for the attempted femicide of his wife, for links to
drug trafficking—Merlo, to maintain and strengthen strategic ties with
entities of the US Executive Branch and Congress; identify opportunities for
bilateral collaboration and facilitate direct communication channels between
El Salvador and relevant political actors in the US; support the organization
of official visits, bilateral meetings and other dealings in the United
States; design and implement communication strategies to position key
narratives of the Salvadoran government before international media; serve as
liaison between El Salvador and global journalists, editors and media outlets;
provide strategic guidance on interviews, press releases and public positions
of the government before international audiences.

**Graph 1. El Salvador 's Funding to LAAG**

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-11.png)SOURCE: Own elaboration with data from Open Secrets, various
years [3]

### Grenada and CARICOM

In 2026, Merlo's LAAG also received funding from the government of Grenada for
six months, between March and August 2026, for 35 thousand dollars. The
contract was signed by Grenada's Minister of Foreign Affairs Joseph Andall and
Damian Merlo.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-12.png)Source: US Department of Justice

The objectives of the agreement included highlighting Grenada's role in the
Caribbean Community (CARICOM). Also strengthening bilateral relations:
improving cooperation in trade, security and economic development between
Grenada and the United States; articulating Grenada's positions: clearly
conveying the priorities of Grenada's foreign policy, including its commitment
to peaceful regional relations and non-interference in geopolitical rivalries;
media engagement: developing and disseminating favorable narratives through
media-targeted communication to generate public support and counter
disinformation.

### Andrés "Andy" Rivas and Miami

**As the Argentine press detailed regarding the Cerimedo case, another
relevant member of the right-wing network linked to the adviser of Rodrigo
Paz, president of Bolivia, is Andrés "Andy" Rivas, who is an adviser to the
president of Paraguay, Santiago Peña, and, according to the Paraguayan outlet
ABC Color, is the "shadow adviser" of Foreign Minister **Rubén Ramírez
Lezcano**.**

Rivas won the 2019 Napolitan Victory Award for the campaign of then Paraguayan
deputy Hugo Ramírez in Asunción, was a Fulbright fellow, and passed through
Germany's right-wing Naumann Foundation, the Taipei Economic Office and
Spain's FAES Foundation, where figures of the right such as José María Aznar,
Cayetana Álvarez and Guillermo Lasso (former president of Ecuador) are found.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-13.jpg)June 2024: Andy Rivas, first on the left; Adrián Cervantes,
founder of Biossman México; Santiago Peña, President of Paraguay; Javier
Cárdenas, of the board of directors of the Adam Smith Center; Daniel Hadad,
founder and CEO of Infobae; Rubén Ramírez Lezcano, Minister of Foreign Affairs
of Paraguay.

As an adviser, Andy Rivas brought the Paraguayan president closer to the
circle of US congressman Mario Díaz-Balart, an open opponent of the
transformation process in Mexico, the Cuban revolution and other progressive
processes. In addition, **the link with media outlets such as Infobae is also
shown in a 2024 meeting. That year, Daniel Hadad** , owner of this media
outlet, **attended the gala of the Adam Smith Center for Economic Freedom of
Florida International University**.

### DMM and MAGA

Between 2021 and 2022, the firm where Damian Merlo worked, DMM Consulting,
appeared as a vendor of the Honor Bound PAC, associated with the financing
network of Donald Trump's campaign. DMM Consulting received 607,552 dollars.

That is why, when Cerimedo's former partner, whom he ordered killed while she
was pregnant, publishes photos with Trump's son, Dick Morris, Cerimedo and
Andy Rivas, it is important to consider that the channels of Latin American
politics now pass through those of the United States, Miami and Trump.

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cerimedo-
network-14.jpg)From left to right, Andrés Rivas, Fernando Cerimedo, Donald
Trump Jr., Brad Parscale, Dick Morris.
